expected_effect: Restoring frontend's prior resource config (limits.cpu 1 / requests.cpu 100m, undoing the 500m/500m edit at 21:10:10 [tr_ec5e968a606a]) and recreating the container should let frontend complete requests again. Observable as: the frontend span rate denominator becoming defined and non-zero in every 5m interval (no repeat of the three no-span intervals), and the frontend Loki stream emitting request lines beyond a single cold-start block instead of going silent as it did after 21:10:11.
if_wrong: Falsified if, 10 minutes after the revert and its cold start, frontend span rate is still undefined/zero and Loki still shows nothing past the startup block. Note two live doubts: container-level throttling, restart and OOM data were never returned [tr_d2052c256486], so starvation is inferred not measured; and Tempo returned nothing for the whole window with a truncated flag [tr_adf228881c31], so if logs show traffic while span metrics stay empty, suspect the telemetry pipeline rather than a failed fix.
risk: If the diagnosis is wrong this is a wasted recreate of the alerted user-facing service, dropping in-flight requests and its in-process cache. Restoring a 1-core ceiling also lets frontend push more load downstream; if the real fault is a saturated dependency, this deepens it. It also reverses a platform-automation action, which may be re-applied and flap unless that automation is paused.
blast_radius: frontend is recreated: external callers see resets for the restart duration. Its five downstream dependencies (profile, recommendation, reservation, search, user) see traffic stop, then resume at possibly higher volume.
